onglets-propos: The bottom bar, sized to its labels. Shown in a frame of at most 360 px — the width the rule was settled on.
onglets-quatre: Four tabs — network discussions are closed
onglets-cinq: Five tabs, with counter — network discussions are open
onglets-largeur: Tab width: the label plus 3 px of air on each side, 48 px at least, the rest shared out. No label is truncated or wrapped: when room runs short, the bar alone scrolls.
onglets-actif: The lit tab is the one for the open screen. Here it is named by hand, since the board is not a screen: 3 px rule above, weight 700, accent colour.
entete-propos: Connection line, “Aa” button to the glossary, title, subtitle. On a secondary screen, the back button replaces the tab title.
entete-retour-titre: Contact group on the gender action plan
entete-lexique: “Aa” open — the glossary is the current screen
entete-note: “Aa” is an 18 px button glyph, outside the text scale: it does not grow with the reading setting. Its pressed state shows under a finger.
connexion-propos: The banner appears once per offline episode; the header line is the quiet reminder afterwards.
connexion-note: The time is that of the last successful read, never the present moment: it is what tells whether what is on screen is ten minutes or a night old. It is given without a time zone, on the phone's clock.
groupe-propos: Name in capitals, counter or pictogram, firm rule underneath.
info-propos: The rule of the place, in one bordered line. Its exit is named for itself and described by the sentence.
info-seule: Only people who agreed to it appear in this directory.
info-avec: This channel is moderated by the IFDD. Messages stay visible for the whole conference.
etiquette-propos: Where a piece of data comes from, what produced it. A tag does not state a status: no role colour, no solid fill.
ecran-propos: The assembly: header, connection banner, content, tab bar.
ecran-note: The screen frame has no showcase of its own: it is made only of what precedes it, and the page carrying this board is itself one. Nesting it here would give two top-level titles and two tab bars for a single screen.
